questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The variety of courses in quantum technology that TU Delft offers.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. There is an introduction week where you get all the information and get to meet other exchange students. Very well organised.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance with course choices was available online.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Semi easy, but pretty expensive. Try to get it via TU Delft (here it is more cheap), but be aware of the deadlines and be early. Pay the housing fee early as this will affect when you can choose your housing (and the best get booked fast). And then also be aware that you need to confirm your housing via the university, also after you have chosen it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Not a big problem as the public transport is good, and the biking possibilities are really great. Living in the Haague, Rotterdam or Rijswijk is fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just sign up to courses and attend (can be how ever many you want). Then if it has an exam (so not only project based grading) you also need to register for the exam, but this is different from just enrolling in a course. Be aware that exam registration has a deadline, but only after the course has started. (This is for applied physics, it different from institute to institute I believe.)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The internation office at TU Delft is very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Got all I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at Mytimetable to make sure your courses do not overlap. This can be very annoying.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Similar, maybe a bit below what I am used to from KU. But a bit difficult to compare as this was a technical university, and I normally study pure physics.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They use soooo many powerpoints, and almost no black board teaching... That was pretty horrible. Also, they are more technical/applied than what I was used to at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Quantum Hardware 2, Artificial Intelligence for Physicists, Fairy Tales of Theoretical Physics, Applied Quantum Algorithms, Computational Physics, Quantum Computer Architecture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Quantum Hardware 2 (not math heavy, but very focused on understanding/getting an idea of the state of the art quantum technology!)
Artificial Intelligence for Physicists (pretty fun project where you can make a cool model)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of things. Much sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depends on what you like, they have everything and it is easy to join.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit other Dutch towns. Go to Leiden, Utrecht, Haag.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: On the master there are a lot of full time international students and they are very open and friendly. The dutch are also very friendly and open, but especially the international ones. Also, there is a lot of group work so this is a good way to meet locals!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Hmm I'm not sure

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Look at MyTimetable to ensure you are not double booked, get housing via TU Delft and be early, register for your exams

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Figuring out what makes me happy in an everyday where I need to reinvent new habits.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: When your studies are stressing you out, it is difficult to be far away from friends and family back home. Also, the studies can be more overwhelming when you are on exchange because you do not know what to expect like you do in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
